claims.text: An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the melting temperature of high-entropy materials.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the entropy of fusion of high-entropy materials.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the enthalpy of fusion of high-entropy materials.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate volume changes at the melting point of high-entropy materials.
High-throughput DFT calculations can be applied to high-entropy alloys.
DFT-based calculations can account for the thermodynamic stability of high-entropy alloys.
Accounting for thermodynamic stability enables calculation of the melting properties of high-entropy materials.
The proposed approach produces accurate melting-property calculations.
The high computational cost of the ab initio free-energy DFT approach may limit its applicability to high-throughput calculations.
Agreement with experimental measurements can be used to test the calculated melting temperature, fusion entropy and enthalpy, and melting-point volume change.
